__scanner_result_dec_normal__: Everything found is on your ignore list. Open the items below if you want to review them again.
__scanner_desc__: You can scan your site to detect unauthorized changes in your WordPress core files, plugins and themes. Everything is compared against the official release on WordPress.org, and anything that differs is listed for you to review.
__unpublished_version_desc__: WordPress.org lists this in its directory, but it has never published version %s. So there is no official copy of its files to compare with. Did you install a beta or a patched build on purpose? If not, treat this as a sign that the files were replaced. Check the version with the vendor, then reinstall it from WordPress.org.
__unverifiable_extensions_desc__: These did not come from WordPress.org, so there is no official copy to compare them with. That is normal for paid and custom plugins and themes, but it means a scan cannot check their files on its own.
__email_default_system_desc__: This email will use the system default content. If you want to customize the email subject and body, please switch to Customized Content.
__free_api_desc__: Enter your name and email and we will send you a free key. Once it is in, this site scans on a schedule and emails you when a file changes.
__wp_config_instruction__: Please add the following code to your wp-config.php file (replace the *** with your app values).
__file_change_detected__: Open each item below to see which files changed. Most changes are innocent, so look before you act.
__server_mode_desc__: You can use this site as the main Register/Login provider for your child sites. Please read %s for the full documentation.
__fluentsmtp_promo_desc__: Stop losing emails to spam or undelivered inboxes. FluentSMTP connects WordPress to your favorite email service (Gmail, Outlook, Amazon SES, SendGrid, Mailgun, etc.) in just 60 seconds.
__last_scan_warning__: Your last scan found some file changes %s ago. What it found is listed below. Run a check now to see whether it is still the case.
__api_key_form_consent__: Provide a valid email to receive your free API key and security notifications. By submitting, you agree to our %s. Your email will only be used for API key generation and security updates.
__api_key_email_sent__: We just sent you an email with the API key. Please check your email (%s) inbox and provide the API key.
__api_key_spam_check__: You should receive the API key in your email. If you don't see it, please check your spam folder. If you still don't see it, please
__autoscan_promo__: Scan this site on a schedule and get an email when a file changes.
__autoscan_active_desc__: You will get an email when a scan finds a change you have not accepted.
__login_try_limit_desc__: If a user fails to log in %1$s times within %2$s minutes, the system will block the user for %3$s minutes.
__restore_file_confirm__: This replaces the file on your server with the copy WordPress.org published for this version. Any change made to it here is lost. Put it back?
__recovery_logged__: Every action on this page is written to the activity log with your name, so a colleague can see what was done and when.
__recovery_secure_desc__: Destroys every session on this site, so everyone is signed out on every device, and deletes every application password. You stay signed in here, and nobody is emailed about it.
__file_change_recovery_note__: If you did not make these changes yourself, treat this as a break-in. Putting the files back does not sign out the person who made them. It also does not reset a password they know or remove an account they added. The next screen does those things.
__reinstall_extension_desc__: Downloads this version from WordPress.org and replaces the whole folder. This also restores changed files that you cannot see. Your settings are kept. Before the folder is replaced, anything that is not in the official copy is moved to quarantine.
__delete_file_confirm__: %s will be deleted from the server. This cannot be undone - restore it from a backup if you need it again.
__file_deleted_note__: This file has been deleted from the server. Run the scan again to confirm it has gone.
__baseline_promo__: A snapshot records these files as they are now, so later scans can tell you if any of them change. Updating a plugin or theme is never reported as a change.
__baseline_when_clean__: Your last scan was clean, so now is a good time to take one.
__baseline_when_unclean__: Take one after a scan you are happy with. A snapshot taken on a site that has already been broken into would treat the break-in as normal.
__baseline_changed_note__: These files can run code, and nothing about the plugin or theme they belong to says it was updated. If you did not edit them yourself, treat this as somebody else having done so.
__baseline_active_desc__: Each scan compares these files with your snapshot and reports any change that was not part of an update.
__baseline_aside_promo__: Nothing is recorded yet. The premium and custom plugins and themes list below offers a snapshot. It is the only way to check files that WordPress.org has no copy of.
__baseline_unit_missing__: This is not in your snapshot, so nothing is watching its files. It was probably installed after the snapshot was taken.
__baseline_clear_confirm__: This deletes your snapshot, so nothing will be watching these plugins and themes until you take another one. Are you sure?
__mu_plugins_note__: These files run on every request to your site, and you cannot switch them off from the Plugins screen. Many hosts and plugins put their own files here, so this list is not a warning. But only reading a file tells you if it is legitimate or planted. That is why they are listed here.
__mu_plugins_watched_note__: These files run on every request and cannot be switched off from the plugins screen. They were recorded %s ago and are checked on every scan, so anything new or changed since then is listed below.
__mu_plugins_record_note__: Recorded automatically the first time this site was checked. If you have since read these files yourself and are happy with them, record them again so the watching starts from a state you have actually seen.
__mu_plugins_unrecorded_note__: Open each one and read it before recording. A file that arrived here without you putting it there is one of the most common ways a way back in is left behind.
__baseline_unit_partial__: This has %1$s files that can run code. That is more than one snapshot can hold, so only %2$s of them are watched. Nothing checks the rest. To cover all of them, a developer can raise the limit with the fluent_auth/baseline_max_files filter.
__baseline_partial_desc__: Some plugins or themes have more files than a snapshot can hold, so part of them is not watched. A clean result only covers the files that were checked.
__recovery_secure_keeps__: Nothing else changes. Your content, accounts and passwords stay as they are. The keys and salts in wp-config.php also stay, unless you choose to replace them when you confirm. So anything another plugin encrypted with them, such as SMTP or payment credentials, keeps working.
__recovery_salts_warning__: This cannot be undone. Other plugins may have encrypted data with a key made from these salts, such as an SMTP password, a payment gateway secret or a stored API token. That data cannot be read again. No list shows which plugins did this. You find out the next time one of them tries to use what it stored.
__recovery_salts_safe__: FluentAuth is not affected either way: the security scanner stays connected to the alerts service, and everyone's authenticator apps and recovery codes keep working. Neither is encrypted against these keys, deliberately.
__recovery_salts_signout__: You will be signed out too, along with everyone else. You cannot stay signed in through this step. Have your password ready and sign back in straight away.
__disconnect_note__: This site sends its scan results to your alerts dashboard, which emails you when a file changes.
__disconnect_confirm__: Scheduled scans and alert emails stop. Your key is deleted here and at the service, and it cannot be recovered. To reconnect, you must register again and confirm a new key by email. You can still scan this site by hand. Disconnect anyway?
__relay_disabled_desc__: This site is switched off on your alerts dashboard, so no emails are going out. Switch it back on there, then press the button below.
__relay_revoked_desc__: Your alerts dashboard no longer recognises this site, usually because it was deleted there. Scanning still works here, and you can connect again to get scheduled scans and emails back.
__scan_without_connecting__: You can still run a scan here whenever you like. You just will not get scheduled scans or an email when something changes.
__optin_intro__: Get an email when there is a new FluentAuth release, plus the occasional WordPress security tip. No more than a few a month, and you can unsubscribe from any of them. We store your name, your email address and this site's address.
__optin_share__: Optional: also send the PHP and WordPress versions this site runs, so we know which versions to keep supporting.
__optin_share_details__: What is sent: your PHP version, your MySQL version and your WordPress version. Nothing else - not your plugins, nothing from your database, and nothing about your visitors.
__relay_reason_removed__: This site was removed from your alerts dashboard, so it has been disconnected here.
__relay_reason_superseded__: The alerts service has this site connected from another place. This is usually a copy of the site, such as a staging or backup clone made from the database. The copy keeps the original site address, so it looks like the same site connecting again. Give the copy its own address before you reconnect it. If you do not, the two sites will keep taking the connection from each other.
__relay_legacy_desc__: The alerts service moved to a new home, and connections made before the move could not be carried over. Nothing is wrong with this site. Scanning here has worked all along and still works. Connect again to get scheduled scans and alert emails.
__2fa_conflict_blocking_desc__: Two plugins cannot both finish a login, so sign-ins get stuck. Please use just one.
